ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.88 (full surge differential) to the rider's original payment method and log the notification failure; remind the driver that a surge notice must state the new multiplier, the revised fare and a genuinely free cancellation deadline.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat messages [F10][F11] and the driver's written statement [F13] contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation; dispute type is fare, so no escalation is required. safety_concern = none.

Facts: GPS shows the actual route equals the optimal route (5.6 km vs 5.6 km, +0.0 km) [F1][F3], so there is no route deviation and RD-2 is not engaged — the whole $4.88 gap comes from surge. Surge rose from 1× to 1.4× [F4][F6][F7][F8].

SURGE-1 notice test: the notice [F9] was sent at 17:14:45, before the 17:16:00 trip start (timing met) and it states the new multiplier (1.4×) and the revised estimated fare ($22.48) — but it does not offer cancellation without penalty: it says "Free cancellation until 17:13", i.e., a deadline already expired at the moment of notice. "Cancellation fees may apply"/an expired window is not a free-cancel option, so one of the three required items is missing → the rider was not properly notified under SURGE-1. The driver's statement that "the app told her ... she could cancel for free" [F13] is a claim contradicted by the logged notice text [F9], and system records override statements.

SURGE-2 / SURGE-3: surge rose, rider not notified → refund the full surge differential. Differential = actual fare − quote = $21.14 − $16.26 = $4.88 [F6][F7][F8]; the computed surge part (1.4 − 1) × $14.05 = $5.62 is capped at the $4.88 by which the fare exceeds the quote [F8]. (For comparison, a 4.4×-mixed calculation using the $15.01 quote subtotal also exceeds $4.88, so the refund is the whole differential.) Booking fee is not refunded and time/distance fare components are unaffected.

Amount is under $10 → TH-1/TH-2: system ruling final. PREC-1: aligns with DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice, refund of the differential).

element_findings.element: Surge notice states the new multiplier, the revised fare and a free-cancellation option (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: The in-app notice of 17:14:45 [F9] states the multiplier (1.4×) and the revised fare ($22.48) but offers 'Free cancellation until 17:13' — a deadline already past when the notice was sent, so no penalty-free cancellation was actually available. Missing one required item = not notified; the driver's contrary assertion [F13] is a claim overridden by the logged notice text.

element_findings.element: Timing of the surge notice (before or at pickup)
element_findings.reason: Notice sent 17:14:45, before trip start 17:16:00; the timing element is satisfied — only the content element fails.

element_findings.element: Cause of the fare gap: surge vs route deviation
element_findings.reason: Actual distance equals optimal distance (+0.0 km) [F1][F3], so the entire $4.88 excess is attributable to the 1×→1.4× surge change [F6][F7][F8], falling under SURGE-2/SURGE-3 rather than RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider was told she could cancel free is contradicted by the logged notice text, which gave an already-expired free-cancel deadline (17:13 vs notice at 17:14:45); system records override statements.
